rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Good day, stranger. This is the city gate. What brings you here?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: The new gate beam needs lifting into place. Are you trained for such work, stranger?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: He keeps this gate secure and expects his orders followed. That is what a captain is for.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: What business takes you there, stranger? A proper reason is needed before I can admit you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: It is. State your business, stranger.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Because I keep my word and answer for my decisions. That is not reason enough to trust you with the gate; give me a plain account of your business.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Well now, this is the west approach to the city gate; the village is down the road behind you. Are you looking to go through, or just finding your bearings?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Well now, that's a generous offer. What sort of hand were you thinking of lending?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Roderic? Fair man, if you give him a straight answer. He can make a lecture out of a crooked one, though—why do you ask?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Well now, the city’s that way—about five steps north-east. You’ll want Captain Roderic at the gate; he’s the one who decides who goes through. What brings you there?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Well now, it is. Makes a fellow almost glad to be standing watch. You come from far in this fine weather?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Because I’m asking you straight, and I’ll answer you straight. I’m a gate guard doing my duty; what is it you’re hoping I’ll do?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Good day. This is the east approach to the city gate. What brings you here, then?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: A hand? With what, exactly? I’m on patrol.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: The captain? Roderic keeps order at the gate. Why are you asking?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Into the city? The captain decides who enters. Go speak to him at the gate, five steps that way.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Weather's no concern of mine. You here for the gate, or just passing the time?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust me? You don't have to. Tell me who you are and what you want here.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh, good day, love. This is the village approach, just outside the city gate—about forty steps north from here. Are you looking for a bed, or just finding your way?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh, love, that's kind of you to ask. I could use a hand hauling a bucket of water from the trough for the kitchen; I'll put in a good word for you with the captain if you do.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh, love, Roderic's a fair man, though he can be stiff as a gatepost. What brings him to your mind?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Oh, love, the gate's north from here. The guards there can tell you what you need to do to get in; if you're looking for a good word, Captain Roderic listens when a resident he respects speaks for a newcomer.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: It is, love. Makes the yard feel almost cheerful, doesn't it?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust takes a little time, love. I’ve no wish to make trouble for you; what is it you’re hoping I’ll do?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: The smithy. If you mean the town, it's outside the city gate, east along the road. What are you looking for?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Charcoal or dry wood would help. Bring me fuel for the forge, and I’ll put in a good word for you with the captain.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Roderic? He pays late, but he pays. I’ve got a repair order for his guards that’s already behind, so I’d rather he keep his patience.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Go east, to the gate. Ask the guards there what they need from you; I don't decide who gets in.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: If you're buying, speak. I've got work to finish.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You don't have to. I asked you for nothing, and I haven't asked you to hand over a thing. What do you want?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh! Good day! This is the smithy's yard, just outside the city gate.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh! Maybe—Tomas is trying to get the new gate beam up into its brackets, and he could use another pair of hands. Do you know much about lifting beams?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Captain Roderic? I don't know him much, but he's the one at the city gate. Have you spoken with him?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: The gate’s about thirty steps that way, north-east. You’ll want to ask the guards there, though—are you going in for a particular reason?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Oh, it is! Makes the forge feel almost pleasant. Are you passing through, or have you come to see someone?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust me? I don't know you either! I was just helping at the forge, that's all—what is it you think I'm going to do?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Good day. This is the carpenter's yard, just outside the city gate. The gate is about twenty-two steps northwest; are you looking for somewhere in particular?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Aye, actually. The gate beam needs lifting safely into its brackets. Have you handled a load that heavy before?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: The captain? Roderic wants the gate beam set safely and done without delay. He watches the work closely; I’d rather show him a sound joint than give him an excuse to blame the carpenter.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: The gate is about twenty-two steps north-west. Roderic, the captain, decides who goes through; ask him there.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: It is. Makes the work easier, at least. Are you looking for something, or just passing the time?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust me with what? I don't know you, and you don't know me. If it's the gate beam you're asking about, show me a safe plan and I'll judge the work, not your word.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Friend! You’re on the village road outside the city; the gate is about thirty-seven steps that way. What brings you here—looking for a place to trade, or something else?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Friend, perhaps. What can you do that would earn its keep?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: A useful man to know, friend, though the gate is worth more to him than any traveller's comfort. Have you business with him, or are you weighing the price of passage?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: The gate lies thirty-seven steps that way, friend; Captain Roderic decides who passes. If you want more than directions, I could use a hired hand inside—show me something new I can sell, and I’ll take you under my permit.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Friend! A fine day does make the road easier. Are you bound for the city, or just enjoying the weather?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust is a costly thing, friend. What are you asking me to risk—and what might you put on the table?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Good day. This is the road below the city gate; the town lies south, and the gate is twelve steps north. You’re new, then—where have you come from?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Nothing I can give you to do. What brings you up the south road?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Roderic keeps the gate. I report what I see; I won't guess at the rest. If you want his measure, he's about twelve steps north.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Gate’s twelve steps north. Captain Roderic decides who enters; speak to him.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Clear sky. No rain on the road.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You needn't trust me. I watch this road and report what I see. What are you after?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Hm. Village approach. Gate's north.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Hm. Nothing. Keep to the road.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Captain Roderic? Keeps order. Ask him yourself.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Hm. Ask Captain Roderic at the gate. Twenty-four steps north.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Hm. Weather's weather.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Hm. Why trust you? What do you want?
